name: 11-train-for-the-forest
objective: Train the lead Pokemon in the tall grass on Route 1 until it is above the level of everything Viridian Forest will make it fight. THIS LINK IS A REPAIR. It was not in the first chain; it was inserted after link 13 failed by fainting, and the level it aims at was derived from the cartridge rather than chosen: pathing the forest with the three bug catchers' sight cones blocked gives no route at four, five or six tiles, so all three fights are compulsory; the ROM's BugCatcherData rosters for the forest are level 6 (Weedle, Caterpie), level 7 (Weedle, Kakuna, Weedle) and level 9 (Weedle); and there is nowhere to heal between them.
evidence: watch:lead_level>=10 - wPartyMon1Level. The address is wPartyMons $D16B + party::LEVEL 33 = $D18C, pinned by terminalgb_plugin_trainer::gen1's own unit test and recorded in the atlas at $D18C as an entry with rom,live evidence.

The threshold 10 is max(forest trainer level) + 1, and the chain from the cartridge to that 9 is checkable in four steps. (1) Viridian Forest is map $33; its header is MapHeaderPointers $01AE entry 51 with the bank from MapHeaderBanks $C23D - both tables located by property rather than recall, MapHeaderPointers being the only offset in bank 0 whose 248 consecutive little-endian words all land in $4000-$7FFF, and the header it yields reading tileset 3, 17x24 blocks, which is Viridian Forest's real size. (2) Its object data declares three trainers, at (30,33), (30,19) and (2,18), each with opponent id 202 = 200 + BUG_CATCHER and roster indices 1, 2 and 3. (3) TrainerDataPointers sits at 0E:5D3B and its entry 2 is $5DCE, which is BugCatcherData. (4) Rosters 1, 2 and 3 are the three parties immediately at that address and contiguous: 0E:5DCE is level 6 WEEDLE CATERPIE, 0E:5DD2 is level 7 WEEDLE KAKUNA WEEDLE, 0E:5DD7 is level 9 WEEDLE. Species bytes were resolved through MonsterNames 07:421E, whose first entry is RHYDON. Top level 9, so the precondition is 10.

This is a derived precondition and not a milestone the game records - Pokemon Red and Blue have no event flag for 'strong enough for the forest', because the game never asks. That is why the objective says the link is a repair, and why the number has to come with its derivation rather than a citation.
